stem: Which fiber optic connector type utilizes a push-pull latching mechanism and is frequently deployed in high-density data center switch interconnects?
explanation: The Lucent Connector (LC) uses a small form-factor push-pull latching design, making it ideal for high-density enterprise and data center switches. Subscriber Connector (SC) uses a push-pull mechanism but is larger in form factor. Straight Tip (ST) uses a bayonet twist-lock mechanism. BNC is used with coaxial cables rather than optical fiber.

stem: What is the primary operational effect of enabling Rapid PVST+ (RPVST+) on Cisco Catalyst switches compared to traditional 802.1D STP?
explanation: Rapid PVST+ (IEEE 802.1w per-VLAN) significantly reduces convergence time from 30-50 seconds down to sub-second or a few seconds using explicit handshake proposals and agreements. Traditional 802.1D relies on fixed forward-delay and max-age timers. RPVST+ does not disable loop prevention or eliminate designated port roles. It maintains separate spanning-tree instances per VLAN.

choices.text: It decreases convergence time through proposal-agreement handshakes instead of relying on fixed timers.
It combines all VLANs into a single common spanning-tree topology to reduce switch CPU overhead.
It eliminates the need for root bridge elections by assigning root bridge roles statically across switches.
It prevents broadcast radiation by replacing MAC address learning with static forwarding tables.
